name: Rooted Minimality Persists along Ample One-Concept Additions
statement: Let $(H,a)$ be a rooted factor irredundantly embedded on $F$, and let $K=H\cup\{c\}\subseteq Q_F$ be ample. Then either $K$ peels to $a$, or $(K,a)$ is again a rooted factor. More generally, along any chain of ample one-concept additions on the same coordinate set starting at $H$, if the final family does not peel to $a$, every intermediate rooted family is a rooted factor.
proof: The added concept is a corner, so $K$ is ordinarily peelable. Every elementary root-preserving image of $H$ is a proper rooted minor and peels to the root image. The corresponding image of $K$ differs by at most one concept; if present, that concept is a nonroot corner and can be deleted before the rooted order of the image of $H$. Thus all proper rooted images of $K$ are positive. If $K$ itself is root-negative, it satisfies the rooted-factor conditions. Peeling to the old root persists after an ample one-concept addition by deleting the new corner first, so root-negativity of the final chain member forces it at every intermediate stage and induction applies.
